transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jamie (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CISO), Evan Brooks (Head of DevOps), Lila Nguyen (Privacy Counsel), Samir Rao (Platform Engineer)

Summary (auto): Security posture discovery for evaluating Redwood in hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Focus on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and retention.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. Quick intros? We'll kick off, this is a security posture discovery, want to make sure we capture Red flag items for your compliance team.
[00:12] Maya: Hi I'm Maya, CISO at Stratus Health. We've got a short list of must-haves for PHI workloads so trying to validate hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:20] Evan: Evan, DevOps, I'll be doing the infra side.
[00:24] Lila: Lila, privacy counsel - I'll mainly track data flows and retention.
[00:28] Samir: Samir, platform eng, I'll be the touchpoint for networking/KMS stuff.
[00:31] Jamie: Jamie from Redwood, I'm the SE, I'll cover architecture and ops. Priya is also joining to help with integration and SSO.
[00:40] Priya: hi all.
[00:42] Alex: Great. To orient: Redwood can run hosted (our SaaS), dedicated reserved capacity, or private (VPC / on-prem). We usually see customers start hosted for speed but many in healthcare prefer dedicated or private. We'll focus on the security controls you asked about: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and retention.
[01:05] Maya: Good. First, can you confirm proofs: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 scope, do you have penetration test results?
[01:15] Alex: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and an ISO27001 certificate; I'll attach the summary and the auditor contact info. We also do annual third-party pentests and internal vuln scans, results summary available in the vendor package.
[01:28] Lila: Is the SOC2 report redacted or full? We typically need redacted copy for vendor risk.
[01:33] Alex: Redacted copy. Full is scoped to auditors only.
[01:36] Samir: On hosted, is there any multi-tenant data separation? How do you guarantee tenancy separation?
[01:44] Jamie: Good question. Hosted is multi-tenant but we use strong logical isolation: request routing, tenant IDs at the API layer, encrypted per-customer keys for storage of secrets. For higher assurance we recommend Dedicated - that provides reserved GPU pools and network isolation.
[02:02] Evan: For dedicated, do we still go over the public internet or can we get a VPC peering option?
[02:08] Priya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; for the Private option we provide a private control plane or fully on-prem stack.
[02:16] Samir: Can we pin model versions and have a deterministic rollout process? We need to certify model artifacts.
[02:22] Jamie: Yes - model pinning and rollouts are supported. We optionally provide image hashes and model artifact signing for auditability.
[02:30] Maya: Encryption: at-rest and in-transit; do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) with our KMS/HSM?
[02:36] Alex: Yes, CMKs via KMS integration for dedicated and private. Hosted supports CMEK for certain enterprise plans; we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM partners.
[02:46] Lila: If we use hosted with CMEK, who sees the keys? Are logs containing key IDs considered sensitive?
[02:52] Jamie: Keys remain in your KMS; Redwood stores key identifiers and never the raw material. Audit logs can omit key material; we can filter PII or key IDs on request.
[03:03] Evan: Audit logs - what fidelity? Token-level logs? Request/response? We need to prove who accessed what model and when for our SIEM.
[03:12] Priya: We have request metadata (caller, endpoint, model, timestamp, latency), and admin activity logs (rollouts, config changes). We intentionally do not store full request body for hosted by default for privacy; we can enable full transcript logging for dedicated/private under contract.
[03:29] Samir: Is there an immutable audit trail with non-repudiation?
[03:33] Jamie: We support append-only audit logs and can integrate with your log collector (Splunk/Datadog/ELK) and ship via TLS. For higher assurance we can sign logs or stream to your S3 bucket.
[03:45] Maya: SSO - we use SAML SSO through Okta, and strict RBAC required. Can Redwood map Okta groups to roles?
[03:55] Alex: Yes, SAML and SCIM available; group mapping to RBAC roles, MFA enforcement, session timeout policies. We also support OIDC.
[04:05] Lila: Do you support just-in-time provisioning or do we need to pre-provision users?
[04:09] Priya: SCIM-based provisioning supports both JIT and pre-provisioning depending on your IdP.
[04:14] Evan: For RBAC, can we create custom roles and restrict model access, e.g., devs can call sandbox models but only ML team can access production models?
[04:23] Jamie: Yes custom roles and per-route/model RBAC. We also have token-scoped policies so you can generate API keys scoped to routes and models.
[04:33] Samir: Data residency - do you have region controls? Our data must remain in us-east-1 for now.
[04:38] Alex: Yes, we support region pinning for hosted and always for Dedicated/Private. We have options for regional deployments and can set routing policies.
[04:46] Maya: About data retention - default retention and purge policies? We need configurable retention and deletion certificates for proof to auditors.
[04:55] Priya: Defaults: ephemeral request metadata retained 30 days; full request/response stored only if enabled, with configurable retention (30/90/365 days or custom) and deletion on request. We can provide purge certificates for deletion events.
[05:12] Lila: Do you provide DPIA or data flow diagrams we can include in our assessment?
[05:17] Alex: Yes, we'll provide a data flow diagram and DPIA template; Jamie can follow up with a network diagram.
[05:23] Samir: Networking - how do you handle egress and allowed IPs? For inbound, do you support private endpoints and IP allowlisting?
[05:30] Jamie: Private endpoints, VPC peering, and IP allowlist for management plane. For dedicated we can provision dedicated egress IPs; for private everything stays in your network.
[05:44] Evan: Incident response - what's the SLA on logging, notifications and compromise? Do you have an IR playbook?
[05:51] Alex: We have an IR playbook and notify customers per contract (e.g., 72-hour initial notification), support for joint investigations, and post-incident reports. SLAs for response times differ by tier.
[06:05] Maya: Pen tests - can we get the pen test summary and remediation tracking?
[06:09] Jamie: Yes, redacted pen test reports and evidence of remediation tracked in our vulnerability management dashboard.
[06:16] Samir: For dedicated hardware, are customers allowed to run models we've trained in-house? We need to bring custom models that include PHI-derived training; are there restrictions?
[06:26] Priya: Private and Dedicated both support bringing your own model binary. For hosted there are more controls - we can support BYOM under a Private deployment for maximum isolation.
[06:36] Lila: Legal/contract - encryption in transit, breach notification, subprocessor list. Can you provide a standard DPA and subprocessor list?
[06:44] Alex: Yes, DPA and subprocessor list available. We'll send the most recent versions and can review any clauses you flag.
[06:52] Evan: Monitoring - do you expose metrics for cost/latency per customer and token audit?
[06:58] Jamie: Yes, per-tenant cost/latency breakdown, token-level billing, and trace hooks for distributed tracing.
[07:07] Maya: Does Redwood do model debugging that might cache user inputs? I want to ensure PHI isn't stored in debug caches.
[07:14] Jamie: We have KV cache and prefix caching for performance; we can disable caching of sensitive prompts and scrub caches. Debug logs can be redacted and are configurable by deployment.
[07:27] Samir: How about model explainability logs and evals. Are those tied to user data?
[07:32] Priya: Evals are stored separately and mapped to prompts. We recommend hashing or tokenizing IDs to avoid storing raw PHI in evaluation datasets.
[07:44] Lila: Regulatory: do you have BAAs for HIPAA?
[07:49] Alex: We offer BAAs for healthcare customers - typically for Dedicated or Private deployments. We'll share the BAA template.
[07:57] Maya: Good. For hosted, are there additional contractual safeguards we should expect?
[08:02] Alex: Hosted enterprise agreements include stricter controls, CMEK options, longer retention controls, and contractual commitments on data handling.
[08:11] Evan: Pricing - is there an add-on for compliance docs and extended retention?
[08:16] Alex: Yes, enterprise add-ons for extended retention, audit log streaming, and compliance support.
[08:22] Jamie: From a technical view, if you choose Private we can deploy a control plane in your VPC with no cross-tenant metadata leaving your network, and you control KMS keys and networking.
[08:35] Samir: For Private on-prem, what's the upgrade process? We need predictable maintenance windows and rollback plan.
[08:42] Priya: We provide scheduled upgrade windows, can do canary rollouts, and maintain rollback images. Customer can opt for Redwood-managed upgrades or self-managed.
[08:53] Maya: Auditability - can we get logs of model changes, who deployed what model, and when?
[08:58] Jamie: Yes, deployment events, model hashes, user actions, and API keys usage are all tracked in the audit logs.
[09:06] Evan: How long do you retain admin action logs? Is that configurable?
[09:10] Priya: Admin action logs retention is configurable; default 365 days for enterprise.
[09:16] Lila: On data deletion: if we ask for deletion of customer data, how do you verify removal across caches, backups, and third-party logs?
[09:25] Alex: We issue deletion certificates and provide proof points: deletion from primary stores, purge from cache, and snapshot deletion schedules. For third-party backups, we coordinate with subprocessors and document retention windows.
[09:39] Samir: Can we get a technical run book for integration - e g network ports, certs, TLS versions, cipher suites?
[09:46] Jamie: Yes, network runbook with ports, TLS policies, supported cipher suites, and cert rotation. We'll include that in the follow-up packet.
[09:56] Maya: For compliance review, we'll need a gap analysis vs our control matrix. Can Redwood help with that as part of the PoC?
[10:03] Alex: Yes, we do a standard security gap assessment as part of sales-engaged POCs for enterprise customers. We'll map controls to your matrix.
[10:12] Evan: We also want to run a short benchmark: latency SLO for our 512 token prompts. Can we get a test harness and be able to run in our environment?
[10:21] Jamie: We can provide a benchmarking harness and script; for hosted we can run server-side; for dedicated/private we can run local tests that hit your dedicated pool.
[10:29] Samir: On the subject of model variants, if your runtime falls back to a quantized variant, is that logged and visible in audit events?
[10:37] Jamie: Yes fallbacks and model variant choices are logged with reason codes (capacity, cost, latency).
[10:43] Lila: Does Redwood do data classification or DLP to detect PHI before storing?
[10:49] Priya: We have optional DLP integration and configurable pattern detection to flag or drop PII/PHI before logging.
[10:58] Maya: Any known gaps? Where do you typically see customer concerns?
[11:03] Alex: Customers usually want stricter housing for keys (HSM-only), longer retention for logs, and more evidence for pentest remediation. Those are common add-ons or private deployment asks.
[11:14] Evan: For network egress, is there a way to force all model calls through our proxy so nothing leaves the VPC?
[11:20] Jamie: In Private/on-prem, yes. For Dedicated we support routing via your egress IPs or via private link. Hosted has private endpoints that can be restricted.
[11:31] Samir: For certificate management - how do you rotate TLS certs for endpoints?
[11:35] Priya: We manage cert rotation for hosted; for Private, customers can bring their certs and manage rotation or delegate to Redwood.
[11:42] Maya: Ok, this is helpful. Any constraints around model explainability or content filtering we should be aware of?
[11:49] Jamie: We have built-in content filters and safety hooks; you can add custom filters and block-list tokens. For explainability, logs can be configured to capture activation traces but those are typically off by default.
[12:05] Lila: Follow on: we'll circulate our security questionnaire (30-40 questions) and expect your answers; estimate turnaround?
[12:11] Alex: We aim to return vendor questionnaire answers within 5 business days; for deeper legal questions may take longer.
[12:18] Samir: Any SLA on key compromise rotation and emergency crypto ops?
[12:23] Jamie: We have an emergency key rotation procedure; if a CMK is compromised we coordinate revocation and rekeying with your KMS and can prioritize reissuing keys.
[12:35] Maya: Great. Let's talk timeline. We're hoping to start a PoC in 3-4 weeks, with a security review and legal signoff in parallel. Is that feasible?
[12:45] Alex: That's typical. We'll prepare the package and schedule the dedicated tech deep dive.
[12:51] Evan: For the PoC, will you provide a demo account with restricted data?
[12:56] Priya: Yes, we usually spin up a sandbox with synthetic data; for dedicated/private we can spin a dedicated environment.
[13:04] Lila: If we need a BAA signed, when does that usually happen?
[13:08] Alex: Usually during contracting, pre-deployment for healthcare. We can share the BAA template now for review.
[13:15] Maya: Ok good. Any outstanding technical blockers?
[13:20] Jamie: None from our side; main blockers will be network approvals and KMS access which Samir will coordinate.
[13:28] Samir: I'll pull together a network diagram and allowed ranges.
[13:32] Alex: Cool — quick recap and next steps. We'll send SOC2/ISO/pen test summaries, DPA and BAA, security whitepaper, network runbook, and benchmark harness. Jamie will schedule a private deployment deep dive.
[13:45] Maya: Thanks. That works.
[13:48] Evan: Thanks everyone.
[13:50] Lila: Thanks.
[13:51] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up over email, meeting adjourned.
